'''''Hedypnois rhagadioloides''''', the '''Cretanweed'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=HECR2|taxon=Hedypnois cretica|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref> or '''scaly hawkbit''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of plant in the tribe [[Cichorieae]] within the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to the Mediterranean Region and neighboring areas from [[Canary Islands]] to Iran,<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Hedypnois Altervista Flora Italiana, genere Hedypnois] includes photos and European distribution maps</ref> and naturalized in Australia and in parts of the Americas (southwestern United States, [[Baja California]] in Mexico, central Chile).<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Hedypnois%20cretica.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:614615 Atlas of Living Australia,  ''Hedypnois rhagadioloides'' (L.) F.W.Schmidt, Cretan Weed]</ref><ref>[http://swbiodiversity.org/seinet/taxa/index.php?taxon=3788 SEINet, Southwestern Biodiversity, Arizona chapter, ''Hedypnois cretica'' (L.) Dum.-Cours.] photos, description, distribution map for North + South America</ref>

''Hedypnois rhagadioloides'' is a variably hairy/hispid annual herb with flower stalks up to 40 centimeter (16 inches) stall, most of the leaves gathered around the base resembling the common [[Taraxacum officinale|dandelion]] except for the bristles. Leaves are green or purplish, up to 18 centimeters (7.2 inches) long. The plant produces a flower stalk with one single flower head or a flat-topped array of several heads. The head has rows of [[Bracts|phyllaries]] that may be very bristly, and the head is egg-shaped when still closed. Each head contains 8-30 yellow ray flowers but no disc flowers.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250005014 Flora of North America, ''Hedypnois cretica'' (Linnaeus) Dumont de Courset, 1802, syn of ''H. rhagadioloides'']</ref>
